title: Getting Started with rsdv: A Practitioner's Guide to Synthetic Data Generation
text: Administrative records, survey microdata, clinical data share common problem: features make analytically valuable — individual-level detail, rare subgroup representation, longitudinal linkage — also make difficult share. Data governance procedures, informed consent agreements, privacy regulations impose friction data analyst. Synthetic data generation addresses problem learning statistical structure real dataset using structure generate new dataset whose rows entirely artificial whose distributional properties approximate original. rsdv R implementation Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) framework (Patki, Wedge, Veeramachaneni 2016), bringing Gaussian copula–based synthesis workflow native R. package designed applied researcher needs generate shareable analogue sensitive dataset, evaluate closely synthetic version preserves real data’s distributions correlation structure, quantify privacy protection synthesis affords. workflow follows four steps: describe column types, fit synthesizer, generate synthetic rows, evaluate result.

title: Getting Started with rsdv: A Practitioner's Guide to Synthetic Data Generation
text: R ecosystem synthetic data generation encompasses several methodological traditions, suited different set requirements. Sequential imputation methods. synthpop (Nowok, Raab, Dibben 2016) widely cited R synthesis package. generates synthetic variables one time, conditioning column already synthesised using parametric models classification regression trees (CART). sequential approach flexible interpretable, synthpop mature support multiple-imputation inference disclosure risk measurement. standard tool official statistics applications, particularly within UK government data infrastructure. limitation sequential CART high-dimensional mixed data joint distribution approximated column--column rather modelled single object; correlations among many variables accumulate approximation error across steps. Adversarial methods. arf (Watson, Blesch, Kapar, Wright 2023) implements Adversarial Random Forests, partition feature space locally independent leaves iterating forest-based density estimator discriminator. tabular benchmarks matches outperforms deep generative models running roughly 100 times faster — meaningful difference practitioners afford GPU compute. handles mixed variable types naturally. package primarily oriented toward ML researchers rather practitioners regulated industries; provide metadata schemas, quality reports, privacy metrics. Rank-based methods. synthesizer (Van der Loo, Statistics Netherlands) synthesises data using empirical rank-based correlation, single rankcor parameter governing privacy-utility tradeoff. approach fast, handles missing data patterns, appropriate settings lightweight baseline synthesis needed. Quality metrics beyond pMSE built . Disclosure control suites. sdcMicro (Templ, Kowarik, Meindl 2015) comprehensive toolkit statistical disclosure control, covering suppression, perturbation, microaggregation, synthesis within unified framework used national statistical offices globally. Synthesis sdcMicro one method among many rather primary product; workflow designed around disclosure risk assessment perturbation pipelines rather generative modeling. Copula infrastructure. copula package (Hofert, Kojadinovic, Mächler, Yan) foundational R library copula families including Gaussian, t, Clayton, Gumbel, Frank, Joe. rsdv uses copula internally fitting sampling. Packages heterocop (Tomilina, Mazo, Jaffrézic 2024) GenOrd address methodologically adjacent problem Gaussian copula estimation mixed discrete continuous variables, though oriented toward network inference simulation respectively.

what: The Gaussian Copula: A Practitioner’s Introduction
title: Getting Started with rsdv: A Practitioner's Guide to Synthetic Data Generation
text: copula joint distribution separates behaviour individual variable way variables depend one another. Sklar’s theorem (Sklar 1959) guarantees multivariate distribution can written copula applied marginal CDFs. synthesis, decomposition useful: can estimate dependence structure data recombine estimated empirical marginal distributions generate new observations. Gaussian copula models dependence correlation matrix. synthesis pipeline five stages: 1. Transform uniform. observed numerical value mapped interval (0, 1) using min-max transform: u = (x − x_min) / (x_max − x_min). endpoints clamped slightly away 0 1 prevent infinite values next step. 2. Map normal space. uniform values passed standard normal quantile function (Φ⁻¹), yielding pseudo-observations real line. 3. Estimate correlation matrix. correlation matrix normal-space pseudo-observations estimated using inversion Kendall’s τ, rank-based method stable maximum likelihood small samples tied values. 4. Sample. New pseudo-observations drawn fitted multivariate normal distribution. 5. Back-transform. sampled normal values mapped back uniform via Φ, rescaled original range. Mixed variable types handled outside copula. Categorical columns sampled independently empirical marginal distribution, preserving observed level frequencies. Boolean columns sampled Bernoulli distribution observed probability TRUE. Missing values handled fitting copula complete cases . default, rsdv records empirical missingness rate column fitting reinstates sampling time. approach models missingness missing completely random (MCAR). Systematic missingness patterns require pre-imputation synthesis; see section missing data .

code: num_cols <- c("age", "education_num", "hours_per_week")  cor_real <- round(cor(adult_income[, num_cols], use = "complete.obs"), 3) cor_syn  <- round(cor(synth[, num_cols],        use = "complete.obs"), 3)  mat_to_long <- function(mat, source) {   nms <- colnames(mat)   data.frame(     var1   = rep(nms, each  = length(nms)),     var2   = rep(nms, times = length(nms)),     value  = as.vector(mat),     source = source,     stringsAsFactors = FALSE   ) }  cor_long <- rbind(   mat_to_long(cor_real, "Real data"),   mat_to_long(cor_syn,  "Synthetic data") ) cor_long$var1 <- factor(cor_long$var1, levels = rev(num_cols)) cor_long$var2 <- factor(cor_long$var2, levels = num_cols)  ggplot2::ggplot(cor_long, ggplot2::aes(var2, var1, fill = value)) +   ggplot2::geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.8) +   ggplot2::geom_text(     ggplot2::aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", value)),     size = 3.5, colour = "grey20"   ) +   ggplot2::facet_wrap(~source) +   ggplot2::scale_fill_gradient2(     low      = "#d73027",     mid      = "white",     high     = "#1a9850",     midpoint = 0,     limits   = c(-1, 1),     name     = "Pearson r"   ) +   ggplot2::labs(     title = "Correlation Matrix: Real vs. Synthetic",     x = NULL, y = NULL   ) +   ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +   ggplot2::theme(     axis.text.x     = ggplot2::element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1),     strip.text      = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold"),     legend.position = "right",     plot.title      = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold"),     panel.grid      = ggplot2::element_blank()   )

title: Getting Started with rsdv: A Practitioner's Guide to Synthetic Data Generation
text: Two mechanisms produce missingness patterns MCAR-based synthesis handles poorly: Missing random (MAR): probability missingness depends observed variables. Income non-response higher among older respondents, laboratory values missing clinician ordered fewer tests healthier patients, MAR. copula captures conditional distributions among observed values correctly model relationship missingness predictors. Missing random (MNAR): probability missingness depends unobserved value . High earners declining report income, patients worst prognosis dropping trial, MNAR. synthesis method fully recovers MNAR without auxiliary information. MAR data, pre-imputation synthesis recommended: missRanger package provides fast random forest–based alternative suitable larger datasets.
code: # Pre-impute systematically missing data before synthesis library(mice) imputed <- complete(mice(your_data, m = 1, printFlag = FALSE)) syn <- gaussian_copula_synthesizer(meta) |> fit(imputed) |> sample(n = 500)

text: Initial CRAN release.

title: rsdv 0.1.0
text: Gaussian copula synthesizer (gaussian_copula_synthesizer()) generating synthetic tabular data preserves marginal distributions inter-column correlations.
